name: FCFS RWLock
listed_description: First-come first-served Readers/Writers lock for POSIX threads.
reason: No numeric comparison reachable. Project homepage http://www.shlomifish.org/rwlock/ is blocked by the egress proxy (host not in allowlist); the GitHub repo's README only points to the man page and test_rwlock.c, the file listing (pthreads/: queue.c, rwlock.c, test_queue.cpp, test_rwlock.c, test_rwlock_2.c, man, Docs) has no benchmark, and three WebSearch queries for FCFS RWLock vs pthread_rwlock found only unrelated kernel rwlock benchmarks. Its selling point is fairness (FCFS ordering), not speed; no directional speed claim found either.

name: fifo_map
listed_description: A FIFO-ordered associative container for C++.
reason: No numeric comparison. README states only complexity (insert and erase O(1) average through std::unordered_map, all other methods same performance as std::map); repo has no benchmark directory (src, test with unit.cpp and doctest only), issue search for performance/benchmark/slow returns two unrelated issues (#1 vector-to-map design change, #2 find() bug) with no numbers. It is a drop-in std::map variant ordered by insertion, and is not designed to beat std::map; the README itself now points to nlohmann/json's ordered_map as the successor.

name: fixed-containers
listed_description: Header-only C++20 library that provides fixed capacity constexpr containers.
reason: No published number against a std baseline. The repo has test/fixed_map_perf_test.cpp (Google Benchmark, std::map<int,int> vs FixedMap<int,int,200> lookup of key 7 among 100 entries) but no results are recorded in the README, the file, or PRs #114, #140 and #143 that introduced it. PR #224 (open, 2026-08-21, by a contributor) reports before/after numbers for the library's own hot paths (FixedUnorderedMap find 1.77 to 1.52 ns, FixedVector insert+erase 23.3 to 16.2 ns, g++-13 -O3) but compares the library with its own earlier version, not with std::vector or std::map. Design goal is no dynamic allocation and constexpr use, not speed.

name: Genann
listed_description: Simple ANN in C89, without additional dependencies.
reason: Directional claim only. README says 'Simple, fast, reliable, and hackable' and 'Fast and thread-safe' with no numbers; the repo (genann.c, genann.h, test.c, four examples, Makefile) has no benchmark, and the README only names tinn, FANN and lwnn as alternatives (FANN described as heavier) without timings. The author's page codeplea.com/genann is blocked by the egress proxy. A WebSearch for genann vs FANN/tinn/kann timings returned no shootout including Genann.
